changes.text: Reliability improvements for busy, multi-station setups - when several workstations are working against the shared network at the same time, batch creation and stage moves are now more robust against rare timing clashes, so what you see on screen always matches what actually happened

Rolling a batch back to the inbox is now safer - each file is returned and its production status cleared one by one, so if the network hiccups midway you get a clear count of how many files came back rather than files that look stuck in Production while already sitting in the inbox

Fixed: moving a job to the next stage from one workstation while another had already moved it could briefly show the move as done on both - the app now correctly recognises when another station got there first and tells you, instead of showing a move that didn't happen

Fixed: regenerating a batch's print file now uses the quantity actually printed (including partial reprints and overrides), matching the totals shown in Batch History, rather than the original quantity from the filename
You can now override the print quantity on several files at once - select multiple files and set the new value in one go, instead of editing each file separately
Custom Order history entries can now be removed individually from Analytics too, so you can tidy up records without leaving the reports screen
The Inbox now shows each material group's share as a percentage of the total metres, giving you a quick sense of the print load split at a glance
General UI improvements across the app for a cleaner, more consistent look
You can now remove individual entries from the Custom Order history - handy for clearing out mistaken or duplicate imports without wiping the whole log
Updated the Minerva print label with the latest layout
General UI improvements across the app for a cleaner, more consistent look

The main screen now shows a quick-view panel at a glance - alongside your last batch you can see how many files have RIP errors, how many are on hold, and how many reprints are open, plus a live production pipeline showing how many files sit at each stage (Printed, Heat Press, QC, Sewing, Packed) and how many shipped today
Click any of these to jump straight to the relevant screen

Holds now clean themselves up - if a file on hold disappears from the inbox on its own (for example moved or removed outside the app), its leftover hold is cleared automatically, so the hold count always reflects what is really there
Refreshed the icons in Custom Orders for a clearer, more consistent look
You can now pick which files to print in a Custom Order using checkboxes - everything is selected by default, so just untick anything you want to leave out

RipFlow now automatically detects when a print job fails inside PrintFactory (for example a wrong material width or a file problem) and flags the affected file with a red "RIP Error" badge - shown on both the Production board and in Batch History, so you no longer have to check the RIP software separately
When a whole batch fails before printing starts, every file in it is flagged and a count is shown on the batch itself (e.g. "4 RIP Errors"), so you can spot a problem without opening the batch
Click the red RIP Error badge to see what went wrong, which step it failed on and when - with a "Copy" button to grab the details for reporting
Rolling a file back to the inbox clears its RIP Error badge automatically - no extra steps needed

Right-click a file in Production (or several selected files) and choose "Show in Orders" to switch to the order-centric view - it expands and scrolls straight to the matching order(s), so QC can quickly see which files in an order still need collecting

Files returning from sewing now go straight to the "Packed" stage after scanning - the intermediate "Sew In" stage has been removed. The flow is now scan, receive (straight to Packed), then Shipped, saving two clicks on every order
Your selection now stays put after "Pass to next stage" - pushed files remain selected if they're still visible, so you can click "Pass" again without reselecting them
Production cards and the rollback window now show the full file name, the same way Batch History does - making jobs easier to read at a glance and keeping the app consistent throughout
Printer and status badges (Override, Reprint, Awaiting QC) moved to the right, next to the stage pipeline - everything else is now read straight from the file name
Hovering over a stage in the production pipeline now shows the date that job passed through it (when it was scanned at that step), so you can see at a glance when each stage was completed
Added short names for materials - you can now give any material a short name in Settings → Fabrics (e.g. "Neraki" instead of "Neraki Waterproof Canvas FR (Water Repellant)")
The short name is used automatically when filing and printing, preventing the "path too long" issues Windows can throw on materials with very long names
Short names are optional - leave the field blank and the full material name is used as before
Reports, labels and the material list still show the full material name; only the behind-the-scenes file paths get shortened
Batch History now opens much faster - it loads your most recent days right away instead of the entire print history, so the screen is ready almost instantly even with months of batches behind you
Search now covers your whole history, including by order number - type an order number, file name, or material and find it anywhere in the history, not just in recent days
Recent days show instantly; when searching further back, older days load automatically in the background (briefly showing "Searching older days…"), with matches appearing as they come in
Fixed: a batch that has just been rolled back, or a day that has been opened, no longer disappears from search results

Cotton workstation now leaves files at the Heat Press stage after scanning, instead of advancing straight to QC - matching the polyester flow. Files show as "Awaiting QC" at the QC station until they are picked up

Scanning a batch barcode at the QC workstation now moves that batch's Heat Press files into QC in one step (the cotton roll heat press has no scanner, so QC completes this step). Per-file actions via select and right-click still work as before
Holds are now shared across all workstations - when one operator puts a file on hold, everyone sees it immediately with no more holds that only appear on the PC that set them

Rollback now returns every file to its correct folder - when a batch mixes files from different groups, rolling it back (whole batch or a single file) sends each file back to its own original folder instead of lumping them all together

Scanning a batch at the QC workstation no longer opens a popup window with a file list - you now see all batch files directly on the production screen and decide what to do with them yourself by selecting files with the mouse and right-clicking

The context menu shows only the actions that make sense for all currently selected files - Pass, Receive from sewing, Send to Sewing, Go back, or Rollback to inbox - and you can select multiple files at once and perform an action on all of them simultaneously
Files that haven't physically arrived at the QC station yet are visible on screen as dimmed with an "Awaiting QC" label, so you can move only the files you have in hand while the rest wait

Reprint and Override badges are now shown separately - a file returned from Production shows a Reprint badge, while the Override badge only appears when an operator has deliberately changed the print quantity
Both badges are shown at the same time when a reprint quantity has also been manually overridden, so the full picture is always visible
Overriding a quantity on a reprint file no longer requires clearing the reprint first - just set the new value directly
Batch totals in Batch History now reflect the quantity actually printed (including partial reprints and overrides), not the original quantity from the filename
The Reprint badge in Production disappears automatically once the job reaches the Packed stage
Fixed: the quantity field in the Rollback modal could not be cleared and retyped using the keyboard
Added partial reprint support - when rolling back a file from Production you can now set how much needs reprinting (metres for linear, piece count otherwise) along with the reason
Files awaiting a reprint now show a persistent Reprint badge in the inbox and batch history until the reprint is fulfilled
Reprint quantities flow automatically into the print job and batch info on resubmit - no manual re-entry
Reprint requests are cleared automatically once a file reaches the Packed stage
Analytics waste figures now reflect partial reprint quantities for more accurate per-fabric reporting
Redesigned the production UI with an updated layout and visual improvements
Added multiple selection support for rollback reason buttons in Analytics
Reorganised the production view into logical groups for better clarity
Added event listeners to detect missing updates and handle them gracefully
Improved Analytics UI layout and readability
First production release
